messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: mondo refactor roadmap
parts:
Just a heads up that Stan's undergoing extensive
remodeling in several of its key libraries.

I'm bringing this up now because Andrew Hunter just
joined us and he'll be initially doing some code review for
us on basic memory management and auto-diff organization with
an eye toward optimization and thread-based concurrency.

Thanks, and welcome, Andrew!

Here's the refactoring plan in play:

1. math (ETA: done, but not yet merged back to master)
Daniel finished the math lib refactoring, including
factoring out tests. All of the functions are being pulled
into their own files, which makes the testing and
dependencies much clearer.

2. agrad (ETA: 1 day)
Daniel's now working on refactoring agrad along the
same lines. All the specialized vari implementations
will go into the files with the functions where they're
used and the generic ones will get pulled out into their
own files along with specialized function implementations.

3. mcmc (ETA: I forgot to ask Michael)
Michael's refactoring the mcmc package to make the
design more modular in terms of integrators, mass
matrices, and adaptation.


At this point, none of our current functionality will have
changed from a modeling language user perspective, but the underlying
code should be much more manageable.

We could release a Stan version 1.3.0 here.

The next steps will build on the above refactorings.


4. views for vectorization (ETA: a few days after we start plus distros)
I'm renaming VectorView to sequence_view and generalizing
it to handle arbitrary types as well as scalars so that
it'll work for our mulitivariate probability functions.
I'm going to generalize DoubleVectorView to sequence_container,
because it provides a concrete implementation with its
own memory.

5. fvar (ETA: 1 day after we start)
Forward-mode auto-diff is ready to bring into the master
branch. It's only complete for special functions -- no matrix
or probability function implementations yet.

I need to write up standalone doc at this point for the C++
API, because it'll be stable enough to announce. We've been
holding off in anticipation of this major refactoring.

6. RNG in generated quantities (1 day)
I've already added random-number generation for the generated
quantities block and Peter's been pushing the actual RNGs to
the master branch as they're done and tested. This is mainly
a documentation and parser error-condition handling effort.
So it'll probably get done earlier.



At this point, we should definitely release 1.3.0 or 1.4.0.


7. RM-HMC (??)
This is the big project Michael undertook the MCMC
refactorization in order to implement. In order to support it,
we need to build out the rest of the fvar lib.


With RM-HMC, we'll have Stan 2.0.0.


Then, it'll be time to think about discrete sampling.

- Bob
